about: The procedural world's numbers (B01, D-game-34). vertical is the range of block rows (y -64 to 320, whole 16-block chunk layers) and the sea level, which stays 32 so the valley keeps its coordinates. climate gives the six smooth fields the world is made of, each a fractal of gradient noise (cell is the first octave's size in blocks, each octave halves it; warpBlocks bends the field by that many blocks at most) sampled every latticeBlocks blocks and interpolated; temperature falls by lapsePer100Blocks thousandths for every 100 blocks above the sea, and snow and trees follow that value against the thresholds in altitude. height holds three splines (points are [input, output]; an input is thousandths of the field's range): base from the continentalness (blocks), rangeFactor from the erosion (thousandths: how much of the peaks shows) and peaks from the ridges (blocks), so height = base + factor x peaks + hills; above softCapAbove the ground rises at half rate and never passes clamp. Terraces shape the steep middle slopes, crags the highest ridges, rivers and lakes are the drainage of the land (see below) carved to a bed under their own water level. Every number is a whole number: lengths are blocks, field values thousandths of their range (-1000 to 1000). Biomes are in biomes.json; no word of Spanish belongs here. regionBlend (B06) is how the land outside an authored region (the valley) is eased into its edge: over margin blocks the ground eases to the edge's height, no trunk stands within treeClearance columns of the border and the trees thin across the margin, the continentalness never falls below a floor that runs from landBias.floor at the edge to landBias.shoreFloor at landBias.radius blocks out (so no sea opens at the valley's feet), the edge's own roughness is blurred over edgeSmoothing.blurRadius columns and the ground eases from the edge's exact height to the blurred one over edgeSmoothing.ease blocks (so the edge does not comb the land into ridges), and each exit corridor is a road of halfWidth blocks each side of the line from (fromX, fromZ) to (toX, toZ), its bank easing over shoulder blocks and giving way to the land over the last fade blocks. Field values are thousandths; every number is a whole number. B02b and its redo (the owner's map reviews of B02): climate.continents makes the continentalness continents, not noise: the plane is cut into jittered cells (cell blocks wide), each block of seaBlock x seaBlock cells holds seaPerBlock open-sea cells (so the sea is 35 to 45% of any 16k square), the rest are land, and a channel of sea (between channelMin and channel blocks each side, varied by a noise of widthCell) runs along every border, so the land cells are continents 5 000 to 15 000 blocks across and the sea is one connected ocean whatever the seed; the coast is bent by two warps (the continentalness's own and coastCell/coastBlocks); the continentalness is the signed distance from the coast (scaleBlocks blocks make 1 000 thousandths) and salt picks the arrangement (23 gives the three maps of the review about 40% sea). The base spline falls from y 32 at the shore to y 13 within about 90 blocks, y -20 by 300, y -44 by 800 and y -54 far out (a deep sea: about 20 blocks deep a hundred blocks out, 60 to 80 in the channels between continents and the open ocean; the bedrock floor is at most y -60) and rises steeply to a flat clean beach strip, then gently over wide plains and inland to about y 90; height.coast fades the peaks out over the land near the sea (peaksFrom to peaksTo), calms the hills there (hillsFrom to hillsTo, hillsFloor) and takes them off the low ground (flatFrom to flatTo) so no speckle of flats and pools lies just over the sea. The ridges are one octave (a ridge line is a chain) with rounded crests (round), the erosion a wide field (cell 12288) so chains run for thousands of blocks, the peaks spline is steep at the top, peakVariation scales the peaks along a range so the spine rises to summits and falls to saddles, and the crags are big. The rivers and lakes (B02c, D-game-34 item 33) are the land's drainage, not a noise field: drainage lays a grid of nodes spacing blocks apart over each landmass, gives every node the level its water would stand at (the smooth ground less the hills' amplitude, height.water.clearance and the valley's depth, in steps of height.water.step), routes the water over that surface moved by a smooth relief noise (relief blocks at most, reliefCell blocks wide: on a plain it gathers the water into rivers that join) and dented where the lake field is high (lakeBasin blocks), and floods it from the sea: every basin fills to the level of its outlet (a lake) and every other node runs to a neighbour at its level or lower, so the water only falls. Where more than sourceArea nodes drain through a node there is a river; its width grows with the ground that drains into it, from rivers.width (the distance across which the carve fades out; the water is about half as wide) to widthMax at fullArea nodes, and its depth from rivers.depth to depthMax; jitter moves the nodes off the grid and bow bends each reach sideways by that share (in thousandths) of its length. A landmass is read whole when a node of it is first asked for (maxNodes caps a world with no sea round its land), so the network is the same wherever it is asked for first. rivers.fadeFromHeight to fadeToHeight, seaFadeFrom to seaFadeTo and peakFadeFrom to peakFadeTo fade the carve out on high ground, towards the sea and where the ranges' peaks add height (a river does not cross a crest); rivers.valley says from what height (from) the water stands deeper under the ground (depthGrowth thousandths of a block for every block above) and how much wider the river is (widthPer100Blocks blocks of width for every 100 blocks above). The lakes' own numbers (cell, octaves, threshold, softness, calm, height and inland ramps) shape where the lake field dents the land. drainage.regionClearance keeps the network that many blocks beyond a region's blend margin free of water. regionBlend: landBias pulls the continentalness up round a region (floor to shoreFloor over radius blocks) so no sea is within 1 000 blocks of the valley, landBias.erosion keeps the ring round it calm (to fromRadius) and makes a belt of rugged land from toRadius to fadeRadius where ranges stand, headwater.distance is how many blocks beyond the blend margin a river's valley shallows to nothing and a lake shrinks to a pond; inside the margin there is no river or lake. pass (B08b, D-game-34 item 6) is the lock of the exit through the east ring: it opens once every lesson in requiredLessons is complete (the list holds all of the lessons the game has today; the validator checks each exists), or at once under the cheat setting, and then stays open; opening removes the blocks of the scene prop named rockfall (the heap that closes the road), and edge is the scene site where the road meets the valley's edge, which the streamed world lifts its wall at.
